sources.title: UC Berkeley CS188: Agents
sources.author: UC Berkeley CS188
sources.content: A rational agent perceives an environment through sensors and acts through actuators to pursue expected outcomes. Reflex agents choose from current state, while planning agents use a model to evaluate possible action sequences. Environments differ in observability, determinism, dynamics, and other properties.

sources.title: UC Berkeley CS188: State Spaces and Search Problems
sources.author: UC Berkeley CS188
sources.content: A search problem defines a state space, actions, transition model, action cost, start state, and goal test. Search trees represent paths through a state-space graph. Graph search tracks explored states to avoid redundant expansion.

sources.title: UC Berkeley CS188: Informed Search
sources.author: UC Berkeley CS188
sources.content: Greedy search prioritizes heuristic estimates of remaining distance, while A* combines path cost and heuristic estimate. Admissible heuristics do not overestimate optimal remaining cost. Consistency constrains heuristic change across an edge and supports optimal graph-search behavior.
